items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of chlorine with hot concentrated NaOH solution.

rubric.why: Checks whether the products of the reaction are identified correctly.
rubric.description: Identifies sodium chloride, sodium hypochlorite and water as the products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving all three correct products.

rubric.description: Writes the correctly balanced equation, Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correctly balanced equation.

items.followUp: Define bonding electrons and explain how a double bond forms in an oxygen molecule, O₂.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of bonding electrons.
rubric.description: Defines bonding electrons as electrons shared between atoms to form a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as shared electrons involved in covalent bonding.

rubric.why: Checks the electron sharing between carbon and hydrogen in methane.
rubric.description: States that carbon shares one electron with each of four hydrogen atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the sharing with four hydrogen atoms.

rubric.why: Checks the resulting bonds in methane.
rubric.description: States that four single covalent bonds form in CH₄.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the four single covalent bonds.

rubric.why: Checks the bond between the carbon atoms in acetylene.
rubric.description: States that the two carbon atoms form a triple bond in C₂H₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the carbon–carbon triple bond.

rubric.why: Checks the carbon–hydrogen bonds in acetylene.
rubric.description: States that each carbon forms a single bond with one hydrogen atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both carbon–hydrogen single bonds.

modelAnswer: Bonding electrons are the electrons shared between atoms to form a covalent bond.
In CH₄, carbon shares one electron with each of four hydrogen atoms.
This sharing forms four single covalent bonds.
In C₂H₂, the two carbon atoms share three pairs of electrons, forming a carbon–carbon triple bond.
Each carbon also forms a single bond with one hydrogen atom: H—C≡C—H.

items.followUp: What is a radical? Give one example of a positive radical.

rubric.why: Checks the defining features of a radical.
rubric.description: Defines a radical as an atom or group of atoms carrying a charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an atom or group of atoms with a charge.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can give a valid example.
rubric.description: Gives sulfate ion, SO₄²⁻, as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example with its formula.

modelAnswer: A radical is an atom or group of atoms carrying a positive or negative charge and behaving as a single unit in a chemical reaction.

items.followUp: Define formula unit and give the formula unit of magnesium oxide.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of a formula unit in an ionic compound.
rubric.description: Defines a formula unit as the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it represents the simplest whole-number ratio of ions.

rubric.why: Checks understanding through a correct example.
rubric.description: Gives NaCl as an example, representing a 1:1 ratio of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example and its constituent ions.

modelAnswer: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
For example, the formula unit NaCl represents a 1:1 ratio of Na⁺ ions to Cl⁻ ions.

items.followUp: The empirical formula of a compound is CH₂ and its molecular mass is 42. Find its molecular formula.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship used to derive a molecular formula from an empirical formula.
rubric.description: States that the molecular formula is the empirical formula multiplied by n, where n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the relationship and the definition of n.

rubric.why: Checks application of the relationship to an example.
rubric.description: Uses CH₂O with empirical formula mass 30 and molecular mass 180 to obtain n = 6 and C₆H₁₂O₆.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct worked example and molecular formula.

modelAnswer: Molecular formula = (empirical formula)ₙ, where n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass.
For glucose, the empirical formula is CH₂O and its empirical formula mass is 12 + (2 × 1) + 16 = 30.
